title: Stage 5: Recover a lost commit
summary: 17:30. Sam ran git reset --hard on the wrong branch and two hours of work vanished. Find it in the reflog and give it a name again.

steps.title: Briefing
body: Sam, new to the team, wanted to discard a broken experiment and ran `git reset --hard origin/main`, but on the branch with today's real work. `git log` no longer shows it. Sam is sure it is gone.
It is not. Every commit made today is still in the object database, and Sam's **reflog** lists where HEAD has been:
9c8d7e6 HEAD@{1}: commit (amend): Add gift card balance check
5d6e7f8 HEAD@{2}: commit: Add gift card balance check
4e5f6a7 HEAD@{4}: switch: moving from main to giftcards
Notice the `commit (amend)` entry: the amended commit replaced `5d6e7f8`, so `5d6e7f8` is an orphan too, but its content lives on in `9c8d7e6`.

steps.prompt: Which single command brings the branch back to the newest of Sam's work? Use the `HEAD@{n}` form.
steps.explain: `HEAD@{1}` is where HEAD was just before the reset: the amended commit, whose parent is *Add GiftCard model*. Both commits come back.

steps.prompt: Sam also had **uncommitted** changes to `GiftCardService.cs` when running the reset. Can the reflog bring those back?
options: No: they were never committed; at best `git fsck --lost-found` finds them if they were ever `git add`ed
Yes: the reflog records the working tree
steps.explain: The reflog records commits. This is the real lesson for Sam: commit (or stash) early, even as *wip*; you can always squash later.

steps.prompt: Arrange a careful rescue that does not risk anything further.
steps.explain: Naming the commit first means it can no longer be lost, whatever happens next. Then inspect it, and only then move the real branch.

steps.prompt: Match each reflog entry type to what it records.
pairs: the tip was replaced by an amended commit
the branch was moved by reset

steps.title: A rescue plan from the reflog
prompt: Turn the reflog into safe commands. Write `RescuePlan(List<string> reflog, HashSet<string> reachable)`:
- Consider only lines whose action starts with `commit` (`commit:`, `commit (amend):`, `commit (merge):`, ...).
- Skip hashes in `reachable` (still on some branch) and hashes already listed.
- For each remaining one, newest first, output `git branch rescue-<n> <hash>  # <subject>`, numbering from 1. The subject is the text after the `: ` that follows the action (two spaces before `#`).
9c8d7e6 HEAD@{1}: commit (amend): Add gift card balance check
-> git branch rescue-1 9c8d7e6  # Add gift card balance check
starter: static List<string> RescuePlan(List<string> reflog, HashSet<string> reachable)
solution: static List<string> RescuePlan(List<string> reflog, HashSet<string> reachable)
hints: Find `": commit"` in the line; then the subject starts after the next `": "`.
A counter `n` that you increment for every line you output.
template: "9c8d7e6 HEAD@{1}: commit (amend): Add gift card balance check",
"5d6e7f8 HEAD@{2}: commit: Add gift card balance check",
"4e5f6a7 HEAD@{4}: switch: moving from main to giftcards" };
"git branch rescue-1 9c8d7e6  # Add gift card balance check",
"git branch rescue-2 5d6e7f8  # Add gift card balance check",
"git branch rescue-3 2b3c4d5  # Add GiftCard model" }, RescuePlan(dojoLog, new() { "4e5f6a7" }));
Dojo.Eq("reachable commits are skipped", new List<string> { "git branch rescue-1 5d6e7f8  # Add gift card balance check" },
